Zucchini purée with lor cheese: 1 tablespoon unsalted lor cheese
Steam the zucchini for 10 minutes; once lukewarm add the lor cheese and mash.
Choose unsalted lor cheese; white cheese isn’t recommended before 12 months because of its salt.
Bulgur vegetable porridge
Cook everything for 15 minutes.
Bulgur introduces the baby to a more textured consistency.
Zucchini mash with yogurt
2 tablespoons homemade yogurt
Steam the zucchini for 10 minutes and cool; mash with the yogurt.
Don’t add garlic or salt.
Beef liver and vegetable purée
20 g beef liver
Remove the membrane from the liver and boil with the vegetables for 15 minutes, until no pink remains inside.
As it is very high in vitamin A, give it at most once a week.
Zucchini purée with apple
Fruity vegetable purées can make new vegetables easier to accept.
Steamed carrot sticks
Peel the carrot and cut into sticks the length of a little finger.
Steam for 15–18 minutes, until it squashes easily between your fingers.
Put 2–3 sticks in front of the baby.
Finger foods should fit in the baby’s fist, be the length of a little finger and soft enough to squash with toothless gums; stay with the baby throughout the meal.
Baked sweet potato wedges
Peel the sweet potato and cut into thick finger-sized wedges.
Toss with olive oil and arrange on baking paper.
Bake for 25–30 minutes until soft inside.
Broccoli trees (steamed)
5–6 broccoli florets (with stalks)
Cut the broccoli so the stalk can be held.
Steam for 8–10 minutes until soft.
Let the baby hold it by the stalk.
Egg and spinach omelette strips
2 tablespoons finely chopped spinach
Whisk the egg with the spinach.
Melt butter in a pan and spread the mixture thinly.
Cook with the lid on over a low heat until both sides are fully cooked.
Cut into finger strips.
No runny parts should remain in the egg.
Banana oat finger cakes
Mash the banana and mix with the oats and egg.
Spread 1 cm thick in a tin lined with baking paper.
Once cool, cut into finger slices.
Don’t add sugar; the banana gives enough sweetness.
Zucchini fritters (baby, unsalted)
Drop small flat patties onto a tray lined with baking paper; bake at 190 °C for 20 minutes.
Baking is more suitable than frying. Don’t add salt.
Baby köfte (baked)
100 g lean minced beef
Make small finger-shaped köfte.
Bake on baking paper for 18–20 minutes, until no pink remains inside.
Don’t add salt or chilli.
24 hours in the fridge; can be frozen cooked for 1 month.
Salmon patties (baby)
80 g cooked boneless salmon
Mash the salmon, checking for bones.
Mix with the potato and dill.
Bake on baking paper at 190 °C for 15 minutes.
Check for bones twice with your fingers.
Avocado slices (coated in oats)
2 tablespoons ground oats
Cut the avocado into thick slices.
Coat in the ground oats; it won’t be slippery and is easier to grip.
Stay with the baby while they eat.
Cooked pear slices
Peel the pear and cut thick slices.
Steam for 5–6 minutes to soften.
Put them in front of the baby.
Homemade unsalted baby cheese (lor)
1 litre full-fat pasteurised milk
Heat the milk until almost boiling (about 85 °C).
Add the lemon juice, turn off the heat and leave for 10 minutes.
Strain the curdled milk through muslin.
Leave it hanging for 30 minutes to drain.
Store in the fridge without adding salt.
As the milk is cooked, it can be given as cheese from 8 months.
Baked egg and vegetable muffins (baby)
3 tablespoons finely chopped broccoli
Whisk the egg and mix with the vegetables and lor cheese.
Divide between mini muffin moulds.
Bake for 18 minutes, until the middle is fully cooked.
Let cool to lukewarm, halve and serve.
A practical meal for breakfast and on the go.
Lentil köfte (baby, mild)
1 small onion (finely chopped)
Cook the lentils with 2 cups of water until they fall apart.
Remove from the heat, add the bulgur and leave covered for 20 minutes.
Soften the onion in olive oil and add it, then mix in the parsley.
Knead and make small finger köfte.
Don’t add tomato paste, chilli flakes or salt.
Chicken and vegetable cube köfte
Bake on baking paper at 190 °C for 18 minutes.
Check the inside is fully cooked and let it cool to lukewarm.
Chicken must be well cooked; it shouldn’t look pink when cut.
Homemade yogurt (for babies)
1 tablespoon full-fat yogurt (starter)
Boil the milk and cool it to 45 °C (warm enough to hold your little finger in for 10 seconds).
Loosen the starter with a little milk, add and stir.
Cover the container and leave in a warm place for 6–8 hours.
Once set, move to the fridge.
Yogurt can be given as a complementary food from 6 months; don’t add sugar.
Fruit mash with yogurt (peach)
Peel and mash the peach.
Don’t add sugar or honey.
Fruit gives yogurt natural sweetness.
Overnight yogurt oats (baby)
4 tablespoons homemade yogurt
2 tablespoons grated apple
Mix the oats, yogurt and apple.
Leave overnight in a closed container in the fridge.
In the morning bring it to room temperature.
Serve with a spoon.
The oats soften and are easy to eat.
Yogurt soup (baby, unsalted)
Cook the rice with water for 20 minutes.
Whisk the yogurt and egg yolk and temper by adding some of the hot soup.
Add to the pan and bring just to the boil, stirring constantly.
Add butter and serve lukewarm.
Don’t add salt or mint.
